title: ephemeral-support-allowlist-ttl-extend-and-audit-gap-causing-overgrant-and-deny-flaps
creator: Leila Torres
description:
Summary: A customer reported two related symptoms after we shipped the ephemeral support allowlist feature: (1) a small set of support sessions retained elevated privileges well beyond their TTL (over-permissioned access), and (2) unrelated legitimate users occasionally saw 'permission denied' when role snapshots were refreshed. Audit logs for affected accounts showed delegation start events but no corresponding delegation stop events, making post-incident reconstruction difficult.

Reproduction steps (observed in prod):
1) Support agent issues a temporary allowlist token via the support UI (creates delegated session with TTL and delegation_nonce).
2) Customer user performs SSO reauth (SAML) shortly after, generating a new assertion ID.
3) Due to a keying mismatch in session-permissions cache (we indexed delegated permissions by owner_user_id only), the system re-used the existing delegated session entry and extended the active window instead of creating a distinct session bound to the new assertion.
4) Later, the async session garbage-collector attempted to revoke expired delegations but hit a race where the revoker path failed to emit audit.stop events when revocation raced with a concurrent manual admin revoke, leaving audit logs with start-only entries.
5) Separately, permission snapshot invalidation took a cached snapshot path that expected a synchronous revocation ack; because the revoker returned early on a duplicate-delete codepath, downstream caches ingested inconsistent snapshots causing transient permission-deny errors for legitimate users.

Root cause analysis:
- Primary bug: delegated sessions were keyed solely by owner_user_id; SAML assertion_id / delegation_nonce were not included. This allowed reuse of a previously created delegation across SSO reauths and extended elevated access.
- Secondary bug: session revoker's failure-handling omitted emitting a delegation_stop audit event on duplicate or raced deletes.
- Tertiary/impacting behavior: permission snapshot refresh assumed revocations were fully serializable; race between async revoker and cache warm path produced stale snapshots.

Impact:
- Overgrant: small number of customer support sessions had elevation beyond TTL; high sensitivity for regulated customers.
- Audit gap: delegation_stop missing from logs impaired forensic analysis.
- Deny flaps: intermittent 403s for normal users led to customer escalations.

Work items / proposed fixes:
1) Keying change: include assertion_id and delegation_nonce in session key and in cache index. (ENG patch)
2) Audit events: make delegation_stop emission idempotent and part of the revoker's critical path; emit synthetic delegation_stop for any stale delegations discovered during migration sweep.
3) Revoker hardening: make revoker idempotent but ensure it writes definitive state before returning; add retries and a one-way tombstone flag to avoid duplicate-delete early-return.
4) Cache contract: update permission snapshot contract to require explicit revocation-ack before accepting a snapshot for a user if a delegation_stamp changed in the last 30s.
5) Migration & remediation: run a one-off sweep to identify delegations whose last_seen > TTL and emit delegation_stop events, then invalidate affected sessions and notify customers with affected session IDs.
6) Tests: add unit tests for keying (assertion_id/nonce), integration tests that simulate SAML reauth + support delegation, chaos tests for revoker/caches race.
7) Backport patches to 2.3.x and 2.2.x maintenance branches and coordinate release notes for enterprise/private customers.

Rollout plan:
- Patch in main branch with feature-flag gated enforcement (turn on strict keying and audit in staging).
- Canary deploy to dedicated infra by 2025-02-22 (low-traffic customers), monitor audit completeness and 403 rate.
- Gradual rollout across hosted regions over 72 hours if metrics stable.
- Execute migration sweep and remediation in maintenance window with prior CS notification.

Customer communication:
- Notify affected customers with timelines and remediation steps; provide session IDs and synthetic audit_stop events for their retention.
- Offer targeted post-incident support and optional account-level audit exports.

Acceptance criteria:
- No delegation exists beyond TTL after sweep.
- All delegation_start have corresponding delegation_stop audit events in the log store (within the incident time window).
- 403 rate for standard flows does not increase post-rollout and flaps are resolved in Canary.
- Backports merged and release notes published.
